lawOfRecord.name: per-course tutor isolation (STRICT SEPARATION)
lawOfRecord.supersedes: the V53 posture that kept course-less threads visible inside scoped rails
statement: A course-scoped tutor (/tutor?course=<slug>) sees ONLY threads created under the SAME registry slug — its rail, its active thread, its synced pane, its fresh-device restore and its clear-all.
The legacy /tutor entry sees ONLY course-less threads (the pilot history).
Scope keys on the registry SLUG, never the display label (ial-chemistry-17 and igcse-chemistry-19 are both 'Chemistry' — label matching bleeds threads across courses).

Server-side parity already of record: tutor_sessions.course_ref is write-once with a cross-course switch refusal (session-store.ts :308-338) — this change makes the HUB client obey the same law it already serves.
A thread created inside a course tutor (including a server-pane restore) always carries the course context, so it can never fall out of its rail.

Cross-course transcript mixing bug retired: the global active thread could previously be adopted by a foreign course's instance via send()/boot (ensureActiveThread) — the scoped active makes that unreachable.
